quote: 14.1 Indemnification by RevMed. RevMed shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Sanofi, its Affiliates and their respective officers, directors, agents and employees ("Sanofi Indemnitees") from and against any Third Party Claims and Losses arising therefrom under or related to this Agreement against any of them to the extent arising or resulting from:
rationale: A counterparty indemnity in our favour is present and materially satisfies the rule. Section 14.1 requires RevMed to defend, indemnify and hold harmless Sanofi and its Affiliates (and their officers, directors, agents and employees) against Third Party Claims and Losses arising from (a) RevMed's negligence, recklessness or willful misconduct, (b) material breach of its representations and warranties, and (c) material breach of its obligations. Because RevMed's Article XIII warranties include IP ownership/right to license, non-infringement of Third Party patents and non-misappropriation of Third Party Know-How (p0545-p0552) and compliance with Applicable Law (p0542, p0564), third-party IP claims and breach-of-law claims are captured through limb (b)/(c). Section 14.3 supplies standard procedure (prompt notice with no forfeiture for late notice, indemnitor's option to control defence, right to participate, settlement consent for non-monetary relief, cooperation with cost reimbursement), and Section 14.5 expressly carves indemnification under Sections 14.1/14.2 out of the liability limitation, so RevMed's indemnity is uncapped — better than the fallback's 3x-fees super-cap. Insurance backstops it (p0603). Two sub-elements fall short of the ideal preferred wording and are noted rather than flagged: there is no standalone allegation-based IP infringement indemnity with procure/modify/replace/refund remedies (instead Section 10.7 allocates third-party licence-taking, with Sanofi holding the first right), and the patent non-infringement warranty is knowledge-qualified. Sanofi's reciprocal indemnity in Section 14.2 is broader than "Customer content plus breach of law" in that it covers Sanofi's own Research, Development, Manufacture and Commercialization of Products, but that follows inevitably from our role as the exploiting licensee in a collaboration/licence structure (not a vendor services deal) and is subject to full carve-outs for RevMed's negligence, warranty breach and breach of obligations, so it is not a one-way indemnity or walk-away outcome. No redline proposed.

verification.notes: No proposal: element-level redline verification is not applicable.

quote: (b) Subject to the other terms and conditions of this Agreement (including the licenses and other rights granted under this Agreement or any Ancillary Agreement), each Party shall have the right to exploit, including license, the Joint Program Technology, without a duty of accounting or any obligation to seek consent from the other Party to exploit such Joint Program Technology.
rationale: Article X allocates ownership of Program Inventions on an inventorship basis (Sanofi Sole Program Know-How/Patents remain Sanofi's under §§1.109/10.1(a)), so there is no assignment of Sanofi IP, data or funded results to RevMed. Joint Program Technology is jointly owned, but §10.1(b) gives each Party an unrestricted right to exploit and license it without duty of accounting or consent, plus a perpetual, irrevocable, fully-paid worldwide licence with sublicensing rights where needed outside the US — so the joint ownership is not the "joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit" walk-away, and RevMed's own interest is further subordinated to Sanofi's exclusive licences and payment obligations (in our favour). Sanofi also takes an exclusive licence under all RevMed Licensed Technology (§3.1), receives assignment of all Regulatory Approvals/INDs/NDAs once RevMed completes its Clinical Trials (§6.2), and each Party must flow down invention-assignment (or, failing that, a perpetual, fully-paid, exclusive, royalty-free licence) obligations to Third Parties and subcontractors (§10.1(a), §3.5). Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording are noted only: §10.1(a) is materially redacted ([***]) so the precise inventorship allocation cannot be fully verified, and there is no separate "Customer Data" ownership sentence (data is handled through the Program Inventions/Know-How and regulatory ownership constructs appropriate to a collaboration). No redline warranted.
ruleTitle: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data

verification.notes: No proposal: element-level redline verification is not applicable.

quote: (i) Sanofi may, without consent of RevMed, assign this Agreement or its rights and obligations hereunder in whole or in part to any Affiliate of Sanofi, and RevMed may, with the consent of Sanofi (not to be unreasonably withheld, delayed or conditioned), assign this Agreement or its rights and obligations hereunder in whole or in part to any Affiliate of RevMed; and
rationale: Section 15.2 meets the preferred position. We may assign to any Sanofi Affiliate without RevMed's consent (p0610) and, without consent, to a successor in a merger, acquisition or similar transaction or a sale of all or substantially all related assets (p0611), giving us the affiliate and M&A carve-out we require. RevMed must obtain our consent (not to be unreasonably withheld, delayed or conditioned) for affiliate assignments and cannot transfer the RevMed Licensed Patents to a Third Party without our consent (p0615). RevMed's reciprocal right to assign to a Change of Control successor without consent sits at the fallback level and is mitigated by the Acquiror Family firewall conditions in p0613-p0614 (acquired party remains a wholly-owned subsidiary, IP and R&D assets stay with the Acquired Party Family, separation from Acquiror competing programs, no Know-How exchange) and by our own option to terminate on a RevMed Change of Control under Section 12.2(a)(ii) (p0489). Critically, no RevMed termination or re-pricing right is triggered by a Sanofi change of control; RevMed's termination rights run only to material breach, insolvency, competing product and cessation. Noted but not flagged: the Section 9.7(a) tax gross-up where withholding arises from a Sanofi assignment to an Affiliate, and the cessation of post-termination royalties payable to us on a Change of Control of Sanofi (p0508), are narrow economic consequences rather than vendor exit or re-pricing rights.

quote: Licenses. Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, RevMed hereby grants to Sanofi an exclusive (even as to RevMed and its Affiliates), royalty-bearing license (which shall be sub-licensable solely as provided in Section 3.4) under the RevMed Licensed Technology, to Research, Develop, Manufacture, use, sell, offer for sale, import and otherwise Commercialize and exploit Products (including, for clarity, any Companion Diagnostics with respect to such Products) in the Field in the Licensed Territory.
rationale: The Agreement contains no exclusivity, "sole supplier" or requirements obligation binding us. All exclusivity runs in our favour: the Article III licences are exclusive to Sanofi even as to RevMed (p0248, p0250), and Section 3.6 and Section 10.x confirm exclusivity operates for the licensee's benefit (p0265, p0424). Manufacturing/supply (Sections 7.1–7.3) imposes no obligation to source Product solely from RevMed — supply is to be agreed under a future Supply Agreement and RevMed must even help us establish our own third-party supply (p0359). This meets the preferred position (no exclusivity on Customer), so no redline. Two inbound constraints noted but not deviations: (i) RevMed's one-time exclusive Co-Promotion Option over a share of U.S. Detailing (p0380) is a negotiated co-promotion right conditioned on RevMed demonstrating resources to our reasonable satisfaction and lapsing if not timely exercised, not an exclusive-dealing covenant; and (ii) Section 12.2(d) gives RevMed a termination right if we pursue a Competing Product in narrow circumstances (p0493), which does not prohibit us from developing or buying elsewhere and includes an election to avoid termination.

quote: Sanofi may terminate this Agreement (A) in its entirety by providing [***] written notice of termination to RevMed or (B) on a country-by-country or Product-by-Product basis by providing [***] written notice of termination to RevMed
rationale: The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, or minimum/early-termination fee payable by us. Searches for "liquidated damages", "penalty", "termination fee" and "minimum" return nothing, and Sanofi's termination for convenience right (Section 12.2(a)(i)) is exercisable on notice alone — the effects of termination in Section 12.3(c) are limited to reversion of licenses, transition assistance and inventory transfer (with RevMed paying for inventory and post-termination royalties to us), not a compensatory payment by us. This meets the preferred position of no Customer-payable liquidated damages. Two adjacent items are noted but not deviations under this rule: Section 9.6 late-payment interest is mutual (payable by whichever Party pays late) and capped at the maximum rate permitted by Applicable Law, which is ordinary default interest rather than a penalty; and Section 15.6(f) bars the arbitrators from awarding punitive or exemplary damages, which operates in our favour. The upfront, milestone and royalty amounts in Article IX are negotiated consideration, not liquidated damages.

quote: Subject to Section 3.4(c) below, Sanofi may exercise its rights and perform its obligations under this Agreement by itself or through the engagement of any of its Affiliates without RevMed's consent.
rationale: The grant to us in Section 3.1(a) (p0248) is an exclusive, royalty-bearing licence under the RevMed Licensed Technology across Research/Development/Manufacture/Commercialisation in the Field and Licensed Territory, and it is not revocable at RevMed's discretion: RevMed may terminate only for uncured material breach, insolvency, or the defined Competing Product / cessation triggers, each with notice and cure (p0491, p0493, p0495). Scope reaches our affiliates and contractors as the preferred position requires — Section 3.4(a) lets us act through any Affiliate without RevMed's consent, 3.4(b) permits multi-tier sublicensing to Third Parties, and 3.4(c) permits subcontracting as we deem appropriate. Successor transfer is expressly permitted without consent in an M&A/asset sale (p0611), and on expiration the licence becomes "fully paid up, royalty free, perpetual and irrevocable" (p0499). Two minor sub-elements fall short of the ideal but are not material deviations and are noted rather than redlined: sublicensing substantially all US rights requires RevMed's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) under 3.4(b)(ii), and the RevMed termination triggers in 12.2(d)-(e) go slightly beyond pure material breach.

quote: (d) Termination for Competing Product of Sanofi. If after [***]: (i) Sanofi or its Affiliates, alone or with or through a Third Party, develop, manufacture or commercialize a Competing Product and (ii) Sanofi or its Affiliates have not commenced a Registrational Clinical Trial for a Product prior to commencing the activities in Section 12.2(d)(i), RevMed may terminate this Agreement effective [***] after it delivers written notice to Sanofi that it is exercising its rights under this Section 12.2(d) unless Sanofi elects in writing within such [***] period to [***].
rationale: The Agreement contains no non-compete, exclusivity or field-of-use covenant binding Sanofi, which meets the preferred position. Searches for "compete", "shall not develop", "Sanofi shall not / will not" and "Exclusivity" return no restrictive covenant on Sanofi; the only covenants running against Sanofi are the mutual debarment/compliance/pharmacovigilance covenants in Section 13.4, and Section 13.3 covenants bind RevMed only. The licensed "Field" is defined as "any and all uses" (p0053), so there is no field limitation on our business, and Section 3.8 expressly provides that neither Party must "agree to any restrictions on the businesses of RevMed or Sanofi or its Affiliates" to obtain clearance (p0271). The functional restraint the planner flagged, Section 12.2(d), is not a prohibition: Sanofi remains free to develop, manufacture or commercialize a Competing Product, and the sole consequence is a RevMed termination right that (i) arises only after a stated period, (ii) is unavailable once Sanofi has commenced a Registrational Clinical Trial for a Product, (iii) operates during the Term only with no post-term restraint, and (iv) can be defeated by a Sanofi written election. The resulting reversion/transition consequences in Section 12.3(c) are the same package that applies to Sanofi's own termination for convenience, so they are not an incremental competitive restraint. The Section 15.2 Acquiror-Family separation conditions in (A)-(D) attach to the RevMed-as-acquired-Party case (p0613/p0614); for Sanofi, p0612 excludes acquirer IP and the Acquiror Family unconditionally, which favours us. Two sub-elements fall short of an ideal draft and are noted rather than flagged: the "Competing Product" definition (p0037) is redacted, so its breadth cannot be fully verified, and there is no express carve-out for internal development or acquisitions in Section 12.2(d) — but as 12.2(d) creates only a termination right rather than a covenant, this does not restrict our business and no redline is warranted.

verification.notes: No proposal: element-level redline verification is not applicable.

quote: (i) Termination by Sanofi for Convenience. Sanofi may terminate this Agreement (A) in its entirety by providing [***] written notice of termination to RevMed or (B) on a country-by-country or Product-by-Product basis by providing [***] written notice of termination to RevMed
rationale: Section 12.2(a)(i) gives us (Sanofi) an express, unilateral termination-for-convenience right on written notice, exercisable in the entirety or on a country-by-country / Product-by-Product basis, which is the preferred position (customer convenience exit, partial termination included). RevMed has no corresponding convenience right: its termination rights are all for cause — material breach (12.2(b)), insolvency (12.2(c)), Sanofi's development of a Competing Product (12.2(d)) and Sanofi's cessation of development (12.2(e)) — so there is no vendor mid-term walk-away. No early-termination fee or penalty is imposed on us for a convenience termination; the exit consequences in 12.3(c) are a grant-back/transition package customary for a license and collaboration of this type, and RevMed in fact pays us post-termination royalties on Termination Products (12.3(c)(ii)C), which is favourable to us. Two sub-elements fall short of the model wording but are not material deviations here: the notice periods in 12.2(a)(i) are redacted ([***]) and so cannot be confirmed against the 30-day preferred figure, and there is no pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts — a concept with limited application to a milestone/profit-share collaboration rather than a prepaid subscription. We should confirm on the unredacted execution version that the convenience notice period is no longer than 90 days; subject to that, the clause sits at or above the preferred position and requires no redline.

verification.notes: No proposal: element-level redline verification is not applicable.

quote: Such audit shall not occur more than [***] in a given Calendar Year, unless for cause, and shall not concern books and records relating to a period more than [***] preceding the current Calendar Year.
rationale: Section 9.9 is the only audit right that binds us on payments/records (Section 6.9 runs in our favour, auditing RevMed and its subcontractors). It contains every material protection the playbook seeks: a mutual and reciprocal right, a fixed minimum prior-notice period, a per-Calendar-Year frequency cap, a defined look-back with waiver of older periods, an independent auditor of international prominence subject to our reasonable acceptance, scope limited to verifying financial reports and payments, an express bar on disclosing our Confidential Information to RevMed beyond the discrepancy report (9.9(b)), and cost borne by the auditing Party unless an underpayment exceeds a stated percentage threshold (9.9(c)). There is no right of remote or direct access to our systems — the auditor reviews books and records only — so the walk-away scenario does not arise. Two minor points are noted rather than flagged: the notice period, frequency, look-back and underpayment percentage are redacted as [***], so they cannot be confirmed against the preferred 30 days / once per 12 months / 5% (or the fallback 15 days / 10%) figures; and the "unless for cause" carve-out to the frequency cap is a customary exception rather than an unlimited-audit right. Overall the clause sits at or above the fallback on its material terms, so no redline is warranted.

quote: 15.5 Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York without reference to any rules of conflict of laws.
rationale: Governing law meets our preferred position: Section 15.5 (and Section 5 of the side Letter, p0671) applies New York law with no conflict-of-laws reference. On forum, Section 15.6(a) sends Disputes to mandatory arbitration administered by JAMS under its domestic Comprehensive Arbitration Rules in English, with judgment enterable in any court having jurisdiction; patent/trademark scope and validity disputes go to the courts of the granting country (15.6(h)) and either Party may seek interim or equitable relief from a court (15.6(j)). This is a domestic, mutually binding US arbitration mechanism, not the foreign arbitration or foreign-venue outcome the rule treats as walk-away, and it applies symmetrically to both parties. The only sub-element short of the preferred wording is the absence of an express submission to the state and federal courts in New York County; that is noted rather than flagged. Note for the file: the arbitration seat in Section 15.6(a) is redacted ("arbitration in [***]"); we should confirm on execution that the seat is New York (or another accepted US location), since a seat outside the accepted list would change this assessment.

quote: All royalty payments under this Section 9.3 are non-refundable and non-creditable.
rationale: Document-wide searches for MFN formulations ("most favored/favoured", "no less favorable", "at least as favo", "best terms", "comparable terms", "preferential", "match") returned no hits, and a full read of Article IX (Financial Provisions) shows the economics — upfront, capped milestones ($520M), tiered royalties with defined reductions/floor, and the 50/50 U.S. profit/loss share — are fixed figures with no obligation on Sanofi to extend RevMed terms no less favourable than those given to any Third Party or to match a third-party offer. rationale: The Agreement imposes no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay obligation, shortfall payment or volume cap on Sanofi. quote: 13.3 Covenants by RevMed. RevMed covenants to Sanofi that:
rationale: Searches for the standard triggers ("solicit", "hire", "induce", "recruit", "employ or engage", "personnel") return no restrictive covenant on hiring: the only hits are a governance reference to "solicited input", the FTE definition, confidentiality recipients, debarment/inventor-assignment covenants and indemnity party lists. quote: 12.1 Term. The term of this Agreement shall commence upon the Effective Date and, unless earlier terminated pursuant to this Article XII, shall continue in full force and effect until the expiration of Sanofi's payment obligations under Article IX or the Profit/Loss Share Agreement, whichever is later (the "Term").
rationale:
The RENEWAL rule is not implicated by this agreement, and nothing in it triggers the fallback or walk-away tests. Section 12.1 sets a single, self-executing term that runs until expiry of Sanofi's payment obligations under Article IX / the Profit/Loss Share Agreement; there is no automatic renewal, no renewal term, and no non-renewal notice window. Searches for "automatically renew", "unless either Party gives notice", "renewal term", "successive", and price-uplift language return no hits — the only "renewal"/"non-renewal" references are patent prosecution renewals (p0098) and insurance non-renewal notice (p0603), neither of which is a term-extension mechanic. Consequently there is no notice window to compute (so the >90-day walk-away and >60-day fallback thresholds cannot be breached), no multi-year auto-renewal, and no renewal-linked price increase to cap.

The rule's underlying concerns — easy exit and predictable renewal pricing — are already satisfied in our favour: under Section 12.2(a)(i) Sanofi may terminate for convenience in its entirety or on a country-by-country / Product-by-Product basis on written notice, plus additional Sanofi termination rights for RevMed's change of control (12.2(a)(ii)) and for safety (12.2(a)(iii)). Exit is therefore unilateral and at our discretion rather than trapped behind a renewal notice deadline.

This is treated as inapplicable rather than "missing": a usable term clause exists, and importing an auto-renewal-plus-opt-out construct into a biopharma collaboration and licence structured around Royalty Term expiry (p0395) would not benefit us — it would add an extension mechanic where none is wanted. No redline proposed, consistent with the instruction not to flag provisions that favour our party.

verification.notes: No proposal: element-level redline verification is not applicable.

quote: promptly destroy all copies of such Confidential Information in the possession or control of the non-requesting Party and confirm such destruction in writing to the requesting Party.
rationale: The Agreement contains a full exit/transition architecture, so no insert is needed. Section 11.6 (surviving under Section 12.4) is a mutual return/destruction-and-written-certification mechanic triggered on termination only on a party's written request, with express carve-outs allowing retention of information needed for continuing rights and obligations plus archival copies — so there is no "immediate deletion / no data return" walk-away risk against us, and on expiry our licences become perpetual and fully paid up (12.3(b)). Section 12.3(c)(vi) plus 12.3(c)(iv) set out detailed transition assistance, know-how and regulatory/clinical data transfer with defined time and effort limits, and Section 12.3(e) requires RevMed to provide copies of materials and "all reasonable assistance" to us on a change-of-control termination. These transition duties run principally from Sanofi to RevMed, which is the ordinary bargain in a licence-back on termination and is not an issue to flag on our side; the effort/duration caps and the [***] time periods in 12.3(c)(vi) are the terms to confirm commercially rather than a playbook breach. Direction and structure aside, the clause set meets the fallback (data/know-how transfer within defined post-termination windows and time-limited transition assistance), and the redacted durations are the only open point, noted rather than redlined.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

quote: Each Party shall perform all Research activities under this Agreement in compliance with all Applicable Law (including GMP, GLP and GCP). In furtherance and not in limitation of the foregoing, RevMed shall use diligent efforts to conduct its activities under each Research Plan in accordance with the terms of such Research Plan (including timelines)
rationale: This is an R&D collaboration and license, not a software/services procurement, so the rule maps onto the performance-standard and warranty package rather than a conformance-to-documentation period. RevMed is bound to a real performance standard (Section 4.2(b): all Research activities in compliance with Applicable Law including GMP, GLP and GCP, plus diligent efforts to follow the Research Plan and timelines), gives a compliance-with-laws warranty on all prior research (13.2(u)) and a continuing mutual compliance covenant (13.4(b)), and gives an extensive suite of title, non-infringement and IP-integrity warranties in 13.2. The remedy path is meaningful and better than repair/replace/refund: a JRDC-supervised cure process with specified corrective actions and step-in/other rights for Sanofi if RevMed fails to cure (p0292), express indemnification for material breach of RevMed's warranties (p0583), and termination for material breach. The 13.5 disclaimer expressly preserves everything stated in Article XIII, which is where all express warranties sit, so it does not swallow the express warranty and this is nowhere near "AS IS" walk-away territory. Two sub-elements short of the preferred wording are noted but not flagged: RevMed's 13.2 warranties are made as of the Execution Date only (mitigated by the closing bring-down in 13.6(a)), and the 13.5 carve-out is drafted by reference to "THIS ARTICLE XIII" rather than the whole Agreement, so warranty-like commitments elsewhere (e.g., Section 4.2(b)) rely on their status as covenants rather than warranties.

quote: 14.6 Insurance. Each Party shall procure and maintain insurance, including product liability insurance, with respect to its activities hereunder and under the Ancillary Agreements and which is consistent with normal business practices of companies similarly situated at all times during which any SHP2 Inhibitors or Product is being clinically tested in human subjects or commercially distributed or sold. Sanofi may fulfill such obligation through self- insurance.
rationale: An insurance clause is present at § 14.6, so the rule is satisfied rather than missing. It obliges each Party (including RevMed) to carry insurance appropriate to its activities, expressly including product liability cover — the risk that matters in this clinical development/commercialization collaboration, as opposed to a hosting or data-processing engagement. It also gives us certificates/evidence on request and, one-way in our favour, requires RevMed to notify Sanofi ahead of cancellation, non-renewal or material change. Two further provisions run in our favour and should not be disturbed: Sanofi may satisfy the requirement through self-insurance, and insurance is expressly not a cap on either Party's Article XIV indemnification obligations. The clause sets limits by reference to "normal business practices of companies similarly situated" rather than the preferred stated figures (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M); we note that as a sub-element short of preferred wording, not a material failure, given this is a bilateral pharma collaboration in which RevMed does not process Customer Data or work on our premises, so the cyber/E&O-driven fallback limits are not the operative exposure. Effectively at the fallback: a substantive, mutual insurance covenant with evidence and cancellation-notice mechanics, but without express dollar limits. No redline proposed.

quote: 14.5 Limitation of Liability. NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER FOR ANY SPECIAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, INCIDENTAL, PUNITIVE, OR INDIRECT DAMAGES OR LOST PROFITS ARISING FROM OR RELATING TO ANY BREACH OF THIS AGREEMENT, REGARDLESS OF ANY NOTICE OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGES.
rationale: Section 14.5 is the only limitation-of-liability provision and contains no aggregate monetary cap: it is a mutual waiver of indirect/consequential, incidental and punitive damages and lost profits only, with carve-outs preserving indemnification under Sections 14.1/14.2 and damages for confidentiality (Article XI) and IP (Article X) breaches. No cap exists elsewhere in the Agreement, so direct-damages exposure is unlimited for both parties and the clause fails even the fallback on the "cap exists" term. The repair keeps the existing waiver and carve-out sentence intact, extends that sentence's carve-outs to data protection, security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud and labels them "Excluded Claims", and adds one short sentence imposing a mutual cap at the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000, confirming Customer's payment obligations are not damages.
